title: Closest to us: Jack's Point and Hanley's Farm

entries.name: Jack's Point Golf Clubhouse
meta: Coffee, breakfast, an hour with a view
entries.note: Our nearest good coffee and a lovely place to spend an hour or two with a stunning view. They do meals too, though it's a limited menu and they close early: around 6 or 7pm most nights, with a locals night on Fridays running to about 8pm.

entries.name: Jack's Point food trucks
entries.note: Low-effort dinner close to the house and our default suggestion for tired late arrivals. They're around most days, not every day, so do a quick Facebook search for the current Hanley's Farm food trucks.

entries.name: The Farmhouse
meta: Cafe brunch and a few groceries
entries.note: The cafe at the other end of the suburb. A good cafe with a small selection of groceries, and they can pour you a beer at the end of the day.

title: Frankton, Five Mile and Remarkables Park

entries.name: Frankton Alehouse
entries.note: To be clear, it's a Chinese restaurant, and a favourite Chinese restaurant in the area. It's pretty good.

entries.name: No.8 Noodle House
entries.note: Our go-to for Chinese noodles.

entries.name: Boatshed
entries.note: Our breakfast pick on this side of town. There's often a queue, so put your name down about half an hour before you want to eat, or phone ahead.

entries.name: Podium
meta: Five Mile, at the Sudima hotel
entries.note: Quite underrated. It's attached to the Sudima hotel at Five Mile, and being a hotel restaurant there's a lot of good food but it's often quiet, which means it shows up on First Table more than most.

entries.name: Wakatipu Grill
meta: Waterfront dining on this side of the city
entries.note: At the Hilton in Kelvin Heights, between us and Frankton. Nice dining on the waterfront without going into town.
entries.todo: Confirm drive time from Hanley's Farm

entries.name: Fergburger
entries.note: They are good burgers. Julian's a burger snob and reckons he can make a better one himself, but everyone will tell you that in Queenstown you "have to get a Fergburger".

entries.name: Bunker
entries.note: We've been before, and it's our pick for a special dinner in town.

entries.name: Ayrburn precinct
entries.note: There's a lot here: multiple restaurants, some of it fancy and expensive, plus a golf course. The easy option is the Bakehouse cafe: no booking needed, just rock up for a cafe brunch.

entries.name: Mantra
entries.note: Good Indian in Arrowtown. Pairs well with an Arrowtown wander.

entries.name: Amisfield
entries.note: We highly recommend it. The food is amazing and so is the experience. It is very expensive, so save it for a big occasion and book well ahead.

entries.name: Rosewood Matakauri
entries.note: A fine dining experience that's worth it on First Table, where they appear regularly.

entries.name: Gibbston Valley wineries
entries.note: Make an afternoon of the cellar doors. You can self-drive, or take the hop-on hop-off wine bus that loops the wineries; it's on Bookme. There are other tours too, but the hop-on hop-off is enough for starters.

entries.name: Sangas
meta: Pies, if you're passing through Cromwell
entries.note: Amazing pies, but the shop is in Cromwell's industrial area, so realistically it's a Monday to Friday, middle-of-the-day stop. You can buy Sangas pies elsewhere, but they're just not as good as fresh from the source.

entries.name: Remarkables Market
meta: Frankton, the big red barn near Remarkables Park
entries.note: Saturdays at the big red barn near Remarkables Park.

entries.name: Jack's Point Track
entries.note: We often walk Rocket and Luna along parts of this track, about five minutes' walk from the house. Proper lake-and-mountain scenery without driving into town, and some sections are fenced and dog friendly.

entries.name: Lake Wakatipu dog walk with us
entries.note: We usually drive the three to five minutes to the lake. If the timing lines up, dog-loving guests are welcome to come along, it feels like part of the household rather than another tourist stop.

entries.name: Hanley's Farm neighbourhood loop
entries.note: Good for families, late arrivals, or stretching your legs after a flight. Not a tourist attraction, just easy, safe and from the door.

entries.name: Jardine Park and nearby playgrounds
entries.note: The practical family option: close, easy, and a good way to let the kids burn energy without turning the day into logistics.

entries.name: Stargazing from the hammock spot
entries.note: At the top of the local playground near our house, up a small hill, three hammocks are stretched into a star shape. On a clear night it's the simple local spot for looking up rather than driving anywhere.

entries.name: Jack's Point Golf Clubhouse
entries.note: Arrived too early, need coffee, need a view? This is our go-to. See the full write-up in our eat and drink guide.

entries.name: Lake Hayes Loop
entries.note: A loop track around Lake Hayes on the other side of town. Active and scenic without turning into a serious hike.

entries.name: Bob's Cove
entries.note: More than a short walk to a pretty bit of lake. The loop up to the viewpoint gives you an amazing 360-degree view. It's become Instagram-popular, so expect people, but it's still worth doing.

entries.name: Arrowtown wander
entries.note: Heritage streets, the river walk, coffee, lunch and shops. Pairs well with Lake Hayes or Ayrburn when you want pretty and relaxed rather than adrenaline.

entries.name: Tobin's Track
entries.note: A proper uphill walk above Arrowtown. Good if you want to earn the view back over the town.

entries.name: Wye Creek
entries.note: More adventurous, with great views. Best for guests who are fit, have decent footwear and actually want a climb.

entries.name: Buzzstop and Country Lane
entries.note: A cafe with honey options, beer and more going on than just a tasting stop, in the Country Lane area with boutique shops and markets nearby. A gentle local browse rather than a must-do.

entries.name: Onsen Hot Pools
entries.note: Worth doing if you can get a booking, and "book ahead" really means well ahead.

entries.name: Skyline Gondola and luge
entries.note: The gondola is about the view, so go when you can actually see something. The luge is outdoors and good fun with friends or family.

entries.name: The Remarkables
entries.note: Close to the access road, warm house, and Julian can give practical advice on timing, chains, lessons and whether the day looks worth it.

entries.name: Coronet Peak
entries.note: Further but doable, good for variety and night skiing when available.

entries.name: Cardrona ski field
entries.note: One of NZ's biggest fields and a genuinely amazing mountain, more of a full-day mission, works well as part of a Wanaka day over the Crown Range.

entries.name: Lake Alta
entries.note: Don't oversell it as casual. It's alpine, weather matters, check conditions before heading up.

linkOut.label: Chains, gear and lesson advice: see our Snow Access Guide

entries.name: Milford Sound
entries.note: A big day, but it feels different from everything else. Choose the Frankton pickup, take proper waterproofs, and assume you'll get wet. It's one of the wettest parts of New Zealand, so rain is not a failed Milford day. It's kind of the point.

entries.name: Doubtful Sound overnight cruise
entries.note: Slower, bigger and less rushed than a Milford day trip. The special-trip version for guests with time.

entries.name: Glenorchy
entries.note: One of the easiest spectacular days. The drive is part of it, so take your time and stop when the lake tells you to.

entries.name: Routeburn day walk
entries.note: A proper day out for active guests. Beautiful, but it needs sensible shoes, weather awareness and enough time.

entries.name: Te Anau glowworm caves
entries.note: Good if you're already heading toward Te Anau or Milford, a nice option for planners, not a tired-day squeeze.

entries.name: Wanaka and Cardrona day loop
entries.note: Cardrona sits on the Crown Range road over to Wanaka, so it works as a day loop: the Cardrona Hotel (we call it the lunch stop hotel, and it's the pub you go to after a day of skiing at Cardrona), the Cardrona Distillery, the Bradrona fence, and the mountain road up to the ski field.

entries.name: TSS Earnslaw and Walter Peak
entries.note: A historic coal-fired steamship across the lake to Walter Peak. Big, slow and beautiful, with a triple-expansion steam engine that made Julian's dad very happy.

entries.name: Dart River jet boat
entries.note: Holly rates this as the best jet-boating experience because it gives you so much more than just speed. The Glenorchy and Dart River setting is the point.

entries.name: iFLY
entries.note: Useful when the weather ruins outdoor plans but you still want an activity.

entries.name: Game Over
entries.note: Indoor go-karting and easy activities. A solid backup for families, teens or mixed-weather days.

entries.name: Clip 'n Climb / indoor climbing
entries.note: Good for kids and active families who need an indoor option that still burns energy.

entries.name: Site Trampoline
entries.note: A useful kid-friendly option when children need to move and the weather isn't cooperating.

entries.name: Silky Otter Cinema
entries.note: A nicer cinema and a good low-effort fallback, but not cheap. An expensive movie option, honestly framed.

entries.name: Thrillzone and escape rooms
entries.note: Good central options when you're already in town and the weather turns. Fun backup, not the reason you came to Queenstown.

entries.name: Movie room at ours
entries.note: The zero-effort option.

entries.name: Bungy
entries.note: If it's on your list, do it here. The hot tub afterwards is the recovery plan.

entries.name: Shotover Canyon Swing
entries.note: Guest-done. The hot tub afterwards makes a lot of sense too.
entries.todo: Verify current operator details before publishing specifics

entries.name: Jet boating
entries.note: Recommend by style and location once we know the rest of their plans.

entries.name: NZONE Skydive
entries.note: The drop zone is basically in Jack's Point and visible from around our area, one of the closest big-ticket activities to us.

entries.name: Mountain biking
entries.note: Queenstown is excellent for it. Tell us your level and we'll point you somewhere sensible.
